title: Account & Access Fix
summary: YTIntel's account flow is now separated, personalised and production-aware: signup has its own screen with a username, successful account creation is shown as success rather than an error, verification links request a return to the live YTIntel app, and core analysis controls are kept available instead of being accidentally left restricted by account UI state.
discord_changes: Fixed account verification redirects so new signup emails request the live YTIntel URL instead of localhost.
Split Create account into its own screen with username, confirm-password and clear green success feedback.
Added personalised Welcome back messaging and hardened Analyse/Viral Lab controls so account UI state cannot leave the core analyser disabled.
changes: Added usernames to YTIntel profiles with a case-insensitive uniqueness rule and a 3-24 character letters/numbers/underscore format.
Added a dedicated create-account screen instead of reusing the sign-in form.
Added username, email, password and confirm-password fields to signup.
Signup now stores the chosen username in account metadata and the YTIntel profile.
Successful signup feedback is displayed in green instead of inside the red error state.

Signup now requests emailRedirectTo=https://mitchloxton.github.io/pinnacle-navigator/ytintel/latest/ so verification returns to the production app when that URL is permitted by the Supabase Auth redirect allow-list.
Added personalised Welcome back messaging using the saved username and a personalised account button.
Confirmed existing private-validation entitlements remain active and separate from the public analyser.
Explicitly restores Analyse and Viral Lab inputs, buttons and tabs on account bootstrap and auth changes so authentication UI cannot strand the core analysis workflow in a disabled state.
Bumped the PWA shell cache so installed copies receive the account fix instead of continuing to serve the previous cached authentication layer.
why_it_matters: Account creation and verification are the front door to a personalised creator product. The app should clearly distinguish success from failure, return users to the real product after verification, remember who they are, and never make the core analyser feel broken because of cloud-account state.
